description:
Dominant phase of the migration under Option B. Three sequenced operations
on the public repo:

1. FINAL CURATED SYNC from private → public, with HOLD_BACK_PATHS reduced
   to the bare minimum (per-user agent config + secrets only) AND
   ALLOWED_ROOT_FILES expanded to include dev-tooling root files
   (.pre-commit-config.yaml, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md,
   _benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py, etc.). Brings _blog/, all source
   files, dev tooling, the new release infrastructure (Phases 1-3), and
   explicitly-approved development assets onto public main as squashed
   migration commits. Working-tree contents only — no private commit
   history preserved. Results Explorer remains out of v0.3.0 shipment
   scope even if repository migration mechanics touch explorer paths.

2. _project/** HISTORY FILTER-MERGE: on a fresh clone of private, run
   `git filter-repo --path _project/` to keep only commits that touched
   _project/. Push the filtered branch to public as a temporary remote
   and merge into public main with `--allow-unrelated-histories`. Use a
   regular merge commit (NOT squash — squashing defeats the purpose).
   This preserves TODO/DONE archaeology per D2a.

3. CUT v0.3.0 from public using the new release flow (Makefile target +
   release.yml workflow). Old automate_release.py is still on private
   as a fallback; it gets deleted in Phase 6.

Results Explorer DOES NOT SHIP in v0.3.0. Any explorer code or
planning artifacts present during this migration remain development
assets only; they must not be described as a v0.3.0 launch, preview,
beta, public release feature, or release-note headline.

Plan file: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/single-repo-migration.md (Phase 4).

anti_patterns.dont: delete automate_release.py at the end of this phase
anti_patterns.why: Phase 5 (dev locus migration) and Phase 6 (deletion) are separate gates; running ahead conflates two risk profiles.

anti_patterns.dont: enable branch-protection's "linear history" rule before w6 lands
anti_patterns.why: the merge commit from w6 is a one-time non-linear event; enable that rule in Phase 5 AFTER w6 merges.

anti_patterns.dont: release a version that overlaps with a prior failed attempt
anti_patterns.why: PyPI rejects, leaving you in a state where pip cannot resolve the intended version; bump the patch number and move on.

anti_patterns.dont: skip the diff -rq inspection in w4
anti_patterns.why: surprises in what the curated sync includes/excludes are the most common way the final sync goes wrong; manual review is the gating step.
release.yml going green only proves the workflow ran; it does not prove the wheel is installable; only a fresh pip install does.
squashing collapses the preserved history into a single commit, defeating the D2a decision; use a regular merge commit specifically for this PR.

preserves.behavior: PyPI versioning is monotonic - if 0.3.0 fails partway through and needs a re-cut, the next attempt is 0.3.1. PyPI rejects re-uploads of the same version.

Results Explorer DOES NOT SHIP in v0.3.0. Do not describe repository presence, migration mechanics, or dev assets as a feature-complete launch, preview, beta, public feature, or release-note headline.
The 9 pre-existing curated commits on public main are preserved untouched (no force-push, no rewrite).
The fallback path (automate_release.py on private) is not deleted yet - if release.yml fails for any reason, the old flow is one command away.
_project/** retains its original commit graph on public; `git blame` on TODO/DONE files resolves to original private-side commits with their original SHAs, dates, and authors.

verifications.command: uv run --isolated --with pip -- python -m pip index versions benchbox 2>&1 | grep -c '0.3.0'

verifications.expected: more than 1 (multiple commits, not just a single migration commit)

verifications.command: uv run --isolated --with pip -- python -m pip show -f benchbox | grep -E '_project|automate_release|benchbox/release/' | wc -l
verifications.description: Installed wheel is clean of maintainer scaffolding
Installability gate closed via the v0.3.1 recovery release (NOT the failed v0.3.0 run)
verifications.expected: 0.3.1 — closure is recovery-complete per release-recovery-v0-3-1; the original v0.3.0 release.yml run (26160520298) is expected `failure` and is explicitly NOT a closure criterion

root NOT in the allowlist are silently dropped — including dev-tooling
files that DO belong on public going forward. Verified gap (root files
in private, missing from public clone today):
  - .pre-commit-config.yaml      # dev guardrail; needs to come over
  - .coveragerc_core              # coverage config
  - .dockerignore                 # meta-file
  - .env.example                  # example env (no secrets)
  - .mcp.json                     # MCP server config (verify not per-user)
  - AGENTS.md                     # agent instructions, project-wide
  - CLAUDE.md                     # project memory (after Phase 7 cleanup of two-remote section)
  - GEMINI.md                     # agent instructions
  - _benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py  # dev tool
Add each of these to ALLOWED_ROOT_FILES in benchbox/release/workflow.py
BEFORE running the final sync. (workflow.py is deleted in Phase 6, so
this edit is short-lived but load-bearing for the final sync.)

Files to keep excluded (verify they are NOT in ALLOWED_ROOT_FILES):
  - .DS_Store, coverage.json/xml, test-results.xml — generated junk
  - evil.duckdb, memory.db — appear to be local test artefacts
  - setup.cfg, setup.py, tox.ini — verify load-bearing (likely vestigial

work_units.notes:
cd /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox
# First do a dry-run to inspect:
uv run python scripts/prepare_release.py --target /tmp/final-sync-preview \
  --no-commit
# Diff the previewed tree against ~/Developer/benchbox-public to confirm
# only the expected NEW additions appear (_blog, dev-tooling root
# files, and any explicitly-approved dev assets) and no SURPRISE
# removals:
diff -rq /tmp/final-sync-preview ~/Developer/benchbox-public | head -50
# Investigate every "Only in" line. Surprises = bugs. Fix HOLD_BACK or
# ALLOWED_ROOT_FILES until happy.
# When clean, sync via PR (preferred over force-push since branch
# protection may be on public main):
cd ~/Developer/benchbox-public
git checkout -b migration/final-sync
# Apply tree from /tmp/final-sync-preview onto this branch:
rsync -a --delete --exclude='.git' /tmp/final-sync-preview/ ./
git add -A
git commit -m "Migration: final curated sync from private"
git push origin migration/final-sync
gh pr create --title "Migration: final sync from private" \
  --body "Brings _blog working tree, dev tooling, release infrastructure, and explicitly-approved dev assets. Results Explorer does not ship in v0.3.0."
# Squash-merge.
work_units.summary: Run the final curated sync (last use of prepare_release.py)

  pip install git-filter-repo  (or brew install git-filter-repo)

git clone --no-local /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox /tmp/private-project-history
cd /tmp/private-project-history
git remote remove origin   # avoid accidental pushes
git filter-repo --path _project/ --force

# Verify:
git log --oneline | wc -l   # should be many commits
git ls-files | grep -v '^_project/' | wc -l   # should be 0
git log --oneline -- _project/TODO/ | head -5  # should show real commits

work_units.notes:
cd ~/Developer/benchbox-public
git remote add private-project-history /tmp/private-project-history
git fetch private-project-history
git checkout -b migration/project-history-merge main
git merge --allow-unrelated-histories private-project-history/main \
  -m "Merge _project/** history from private (TODO/DONE archaeology preserved)"

# Verify:
git log --graph --oneline | head -20   # should show two roots merging
git log --oneline -- _project/TODO/ | head -5   # original SHAs preserved
git blame _project/TODO/main/active/single-repo-migration-phase-4-test-release-with-new-flow.yaml | head

git push origin migration/project-history-merge
gh pr create --title "Migration: merge _project/** history (preserve TODO/DONE archaeology)" \
  --body "Filter-merged from private. Use a regular MERGE COMMIT not squash — squashing defeats the purpose."

# IMPORTANT: this PR is the one explicit exception to the squash-merge
# convention (D5). Use "Create a merge commit" in the GitHub UI, NOT
# "Squash and merge". If branch protection enforces squash-only at
# this point, temporarily disable it for this PR.
work_units.summary: Merge _project/** history into public main with --allow-unrelated-histories

work_units.notes:
CLOSED 2026-07-09 as recovery-complete via `release-recovery-v0-3-1`.
Immutable `0.3.0` was never re-tagged or re-uploaded; the installability
gate is satisfied by the later monotonic `v0.3.1`:
  - `release.yml` run 29055922350 (tag `v0.3.1`) concluded `success`,
    including every `test-installation` job across ubuntu/macos/windows.
  - `pip index versions benchbox` lists `0.3.1` as available/latest.
  - `uv run --isolated --no-project --with 'benchbox==0.3.1' -- python -c 'import benchbox; print(benchbox.__version__)'`
    prints `0.3.1`; pandas is absent from the 29 resolved packages.
  - `pip show -f benchbox` shows zero maintainer-scaffolding entries.
`0.3.0` remains permanently broken on PyPI by design; it is superseded,
not repaired.

---- original blocker record (2026-05-25) ----

Blocked as of 2026-05-25. The publish half succeeded, but the
installability half failed and cannot be repaired in-place because
PyPI rejects replacement uploads for an existing version.

Evidence:
  - `gh run list --repo joeharris76/BenchBox --workflow=release.yml --limit 1`
    returned run `26160520298`, conclusion `failure`.
  - `gh run view 26160520298 --repo joeharris76/BenchBox --json jobs`
    showed build, PyPI publish, and GitHub release jobs succeeded.
  - The same run showed all `test-installation` jobs failed.
  - `uv run --isolated --no-project --with 'benchbox==0.3.0' -- python -c 'import benchbox; print(benchbox.__version__)'`
    fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'`.

Recovery path:
  - Do not re-tag or re-upload `0.3.0`.
  - Complete `release-recovery-v0-3-1`; if its `v0.3.1` release
    passes clean PyPI install/import, record that evidence here and
    close this work item as recovery-complete rather than pretending
    immutable `0.3.0` became installable.
work_units.summary: Verify the release published to PyPI and is installable
